##### Project general facts

The Vault by Imtiaz is a boutique commercial building that combines premium office spaces with ground-floor retail units in a compact, highly considered setting. A fully glazed façade, a distinctive bronze-toned form and a refined palette of materials give the building a strong visual presence and a calm, exclusive character. The office floors are planned around flexible, modular configurations, allowing companies of different sizes to shape their workspace around the way they operate.

Arrival begins in a reception lobby with a lobby lounge and café, creating a welcoming setting for meetings, coffee and a change of pace during the working day. At roof level, a communal terrace brings together a lounge and pantry, a relaxation lounge, a social lounge, a recreation zone and a refreshment bar, giving tenants and their guests a place to unwind and connect beyond the office.

Inside, floor-to-ceiling glazing draws natural daylight deep into every office space and frames open views across the surrounding district. Sophisticated finishes, rich textures and warm natural tones create an atmosphere of elegance and comfort, while the open floor plates leave each business free to arrange its own layout.

##### Location description and benefits

Majan is a growing mixed-use district within Dubailand, set between Al Barari, Wadi Al Safa and the leisure attractions of the city's southeastern corridor. The neighbourhood combines residential communities, commercial plots and community retail, and benefits from a central position between the established business hubs and the expanding residential suburbs of Dubai.

Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road runs alongside the district, while Al Khail Road and Emirates Road provide fast links to Downtown Dubai, DIFC and Dubai International Airport. Al Barari, IMG Worlds of Adventure, Global Village, Silicon Central Mall and Dubai Hills Mall are all within a short drive, giving workers and visitors easy access to dining, shopping and entertainment.

Strong residential growth across Dubailand and the surrounding communities is creating rising demand for local offices, clinics, showrooms and service businesses close to where people live. Freehold ownership for international investors and a limited supply of boutique commercial space in the area support steady leasing demand and long-term capital appreciation.
